title: Design and Simulated Performance of a Low-Cost Manual Wheat Thresher for Smallholder Farmers in Developing Regions
content: Smallholder wheat farmers thresh by flail: slow work, and tiring. This paper presents the mechanical design of a hand-cranked wheat thresher for smallholder farming systems in developing regions and estimates its performance using a first-principles simulation model. Drum: 300 mm rasp-bar, 400 mm long, 6 bars, 12 mm drum-concave clearance, 4:1 chain drive from a 60 rpm hand crank. Design grain: wheat, 30 g thousand-kernel weight, 7.0 × 3.3 × 3.0 mm, 12.5% moisture. The model is calibrated on two published anchors — 95% threshing efficiency at 11.0 m/s drum speed (Afolabi et al., 2021), and grain-damage data (Imanmehr, 2015). Under base settings the drum turns at 240 rpm, 3.77 m/s at the rim, and gives 80.2% threshing efficiency (SIMULATED), 0.05% grain damage (SIMULATED), and 15.9 kg/h clean grain (SIMULATED) — all inside a sustained one-hand cranking limit of 54 W. Clean-grain output ranges from 7.1 to 21.2 kg/h (SIMULATED) when drum speed, crank power, residence time, rubbing rate, specific energy, cleaning efficiency, and clearance vary. Materials and labour: about USD 50 (SIMULATED). No prototype was built, and every performance value here is a simulated estimate, not a measurement.
